answer:
**Final answer: 36% — 63 of 175 miRNAs (63/175 = 36.00%) show significant differential expression (two-sided Welch's t-test on raw Ct, available-case, unadjusted p < 0.05).**

**1. Headline (primary, as approved)**
- 63/175 = 36.00%. All 175 miRNAs were testable — confirmed from the run: min valid values per group across all rows was 8 (patients) / 7 (controls), so zero miRNAs were excluded.
- The full 63-miRNA table (mean/median Ct per group, ΔCt, t, raw p) is in `results_per_miRNA_named.csv`; top and bottom by p:
  - hsa-miR-20b: 30.94 vs 32.62 (ΔCt −1.68), t=−4.43, p=0.0005
  - hsa-miR-92a: 23.39 vs 24.54, t=−4.09, p=0.0007
  - hsa-miR-1974: p=0.0010; hsa-miR-532-5p: p=0.0011; hsa-miR-222: p=0.0014 … hsa-miR-10a: +0.83, t=2.13, p=0.0480; hsa-miR-451: p=0.0481; hsa-miR-99a: p=0.0495
- Directionality: 62/63 significant miRNAs have lower Ct (higher abundance) in patients; only hsa-miR-10a is higher-Ct in patients.

**2. Sensitivity analyses**
- (a) Mann–Whitney U, same available-case basis, denominator 175: 59/175 = 33.71%.
- (b) Complete-case denominator (161 rows without NaN): Welch 59/161 = 36.65% (MWU: 56/161 = 34.78%). Note 4 of the 63 significant miRNAs contain missing values (hsa-miR-106b*, hsa-miR-18a*, hsa-miR-29b-2*, hsa-miR-10a), so 59 of them lie on complete rows.

**3. Primary vs sensitivity discrepancy**
- Welch ∩ MWU overlap: 56. 10 flips total (not large): Welch-only significant = hsa-let-7b, hsa-miR-10a, hsa-miR-151-5p, hsa-miR-26a, hsa-miR-30e*, hsa-miR-495, hsa-miR-99a (all Welch p 0.038–0.050 vs MWU p 0.055–0.104); MWU-only = hsa-miR-125a-5p, hsa-miR-320b, hsa-miR-885-5p (Welch p 0.050–0.070).
- Only one flip involves a missing-Ct row: hsa-miR-10a (1 missing control; Welch p=0.048 vs MWU p=0.055) — borderline either way, so missingness drives at most this single flip. All other flips are ordinary p≈0.04–0.07 borderline cases where parametric vs rank-based tails disagree.

**4. Normality/variance sanity for the 63 significant miRNAs**
- Shapiro–Wilk over the 126 groups: 8 at p<0.05, 4 at p<0.01 (min p=0.0011) — i.e., ~87% of groups show no detectable non-normality at n=10 (weak power acknowledged).
- |skew| > 1 in 10/126 groups (max |skew| = 2.02, hsa-miR-10a's already borderline-high-Ct group).
- No degenerate variance: minimum within-group SD among significant rows = 0.367 Ct; 0 rows with SD < 0.2.
- Levene p<0.05 in 10/63 rows — handled by Welch by design. Overall Welch is a defensible primary choice; the rank-based alternative shifts the headline by 4 miRNAs (2.3 percentage points).

**5. BIFF8 parser diagnostics**
- Independent raw-record rescan (separate from the DataFrame pipeline): 3,478 NUMBER cells + 22 LABELSST "NAN" cells in the data area = 3,500 = 175×20 exactly; 218 total LABELSST = 175 miRNA names + 20 sample headers + 1 title + 22 "NAN" ✓.
- All 3,478 raw numeric values match the tested DataFrame cell-by-cell (tolerance 1e−12, mismatches: 0); the 22 DataFrame NaN positions are identical to the 22 "NAN" string cells; every value fed to the tests is a float (3,478 finite + 22 NaN, no strings).
- Spot-checks vs raw records: hsa-let-7a row 2 (e.g., 29.188624, 29.333341, …), hsa-miR-95 row 174 (incl. 'NAN' at P_5 and C_20), hsa-miR-99b row 176 — all exact matches. No RK records existed in the data area, avoiding RK-decoding risk entirely.

Limitations: n=10/group gives weak normality-test power and borderline p's are test-sensitive; the headline is 36.00% under the approved Welch/available-case/175-denominator spec (range across all four variants: 33.71–36.65%).
